ForestFireR

R package simulating a two-species vegetation system in which fire mediates the competition between a native species and an invader. The same continuous-time transition rules are simulated three ways: on an explicit lattice with the Gillespie algorithm, as the deterministic well-mixed (mean-field) limit, and as the well-mixed stochastic process at a finite population size. The engine is written in C++ and exposed to R through Rcpp, with an interface built around dimensionless parameters (xi, eta, p) for fire spread, post-fire regrowth and the clustering of the initial landscape.

The model is documented inside the package: help("ForestFireR-model") defines the five states, every transition and its rate, the dimensionless parametrization, the baseline parameter set and the fire-mediated invasion mechanism it encodes, the mean-field equations, and what differs between the three engines.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("EcoComplex/ForestFireR")

Quick start 

library(ForestFireR)

# Deterministic well-mixed limit
mf <- simulate_mean_field(T = 200, n1_0 = 0.9, n2_0 = 0.1)
plot(mf$time, mf$n1, type = "l", col = "forestgreen", ylim = c(0, 1),
     xlab = "time (years)", ylab = "density")
lines(mf$time, mf$n2, col = "firebrick")

# Lattice simulation, 10 per cent invader clustered in one patch
sp <- simulate_spatial(T = 200, L = 100, density2 = 0.1, p = 1,
                       seed = 1, record_dt = 1)
c(native = sp$n1, invader = sp$n2)

# Baseline parameters, and the probability-to-rate conversion
default_rates()
xi2lambda(0.6, 1e6)

What the package provides

function purpose
generate_landscape() initial lattice: one species placed over another with density and clustering p
generate_landscape_layers() initial lattice built from a sequence of placements over an arbitrary fill state
simulate_spatial() lattice Gillespie simulation
simulate_spatial_from_grid() same, starting from a supplied grid
simulate_mean_field() deterministic well-mixed limit
simulate_mean_field_stochastic() well-mixed stochastic process at population size N
simulate_spatial_movie() render a run as a video or animated GIF
default_rates(), xi2lambda(), eta2lambda() baseline parameters and the dimensionless conversion
FF_STATE the grid’s state codes

Recording options: record_dt for trajectories, record_grid for initial and final grids, capture_fire_snapshots for grids captured while a fire is actually burning (a single outbreak resolves in about an hour of simulated time against decades of vegetation dynamics, so a fixed-time snapshot essentially never lands on one). Every simulate function takes its own seed; the engine’s generator is std::mt19937_64, independent of R’s.

Two things to know when building initial conditions with generate_landscape_layers():

  • Native-extinction early stop. The Gillespie loop treats native density below 0.0001 as extinction and ends the run there. That is right whenever the landscape starts with native vegetation, and wrong for a grid built without any (a fire-over-invader domain, say), where n1 is 0 from the first step. Pass check_extinction = FALSE to simulate_spatial_from_grid() for those.
  • Layer density budget. A layer’s target (density * L*L cells) can exceed what is left in its background state. The layer then stops early rather than searching for an unreachable target, and prints how many cells it actually placed.

Worked scripts

Installed with the package:

list.files(system.file("examples", package = "ForestFireR"))
#> "01_trajectories_meanfield_vs_spatial.R"  # the three engines side by side
#> "02_landscape_heterogeneity.R"            # clustering of the initial landscape
#> "03_phase_diagram_xi_eta_sweep.R"         # (xi_inv, eta_inv) phase diagram

Every function’s help page also carries runnable examples, including the reduced-dynamics recipes (post-fire regrowth alone, fire spread alone).

Behaviour of the implementation

Starting from 10 per cent invader and the baseline parameters (xi_nat = 0.5, xi_inv = eta_inv = 0.6, eta_nat = 0) over 200 years:

  • Mean field (n1_0 = 0.9, n2_0 = 0.1): native declines from 0.90 to 0.079 while the invader grows from 0.10 to 0.613.
  • Lattice (L = 100, density2 = 0.1, p = 1, seed = 1): native ends at 0.050 and the invader at 0.675; the same run with a scattered invader (p = 0) ends at 0.057 native and 0.336 invader, the rest of the grid still unoccupied post-fire ground.
  • Well mixed, stochastic (N = 10000): the invasion does not take off (native 0.971, invader 0.029 at T = 200). Fire here is a discrete, rare event, whereas the deterministic limit carries a residual burning density of order 1e-11 at all times, which keeps the feedback running; without fire the native species out-replaces the invader by construction.

Sweeping xi_inv and eta_inv (inst/examples/03_phase_diagram_xi_eta_sweep.R) maps the transition to native extinction over the plane of the two fire-mediated advantages.

Mass conservation (n1+n2+n3+n4+n5 = 1) holds to floating-point precision in all three engines: the largest deviation over a recorded L = 100, T = 200 trajectory is 1.1e-16. The testthat suite checks exact, a priori known outcomes (null dynamics, single-species colonization, isolated fire burnout, ignition switched off, reproducibility, mass conservation, the xi/eta conversion, and the random stream itself).

Performance

Measured on an 8-core laptop with the default sum-tree engine (engine = "tree"), median of three runs:

run wall time
simulate_spatial(T = 200, L = 100) 0.05 s
simulate_spatial(T = 200, L = 200) 0.24 s
simulate_spatial(T = 200, L = 200, xi_inv = 0.9, eta_inv = 0.9) 0.37 s
simulate_spatial(T = 1000, L = 200) 0.55 s
simulate_mean_field(T = 300) 0.004 s
simulate_mean_field_stochastic(T = 200, N = 10000) 0.001 s

Runtime grows with the number of Gillespie events, so with grid size, time horizon and with parameters that keep fires burning. record_dt = -1 (final state only) is the cheapest option for parameter sweeps. engine = "linear" reproduces runs made with ForestFireR < 0.7.0 and is orders of magnitude slower on large grids.

Citation

The package is archived on Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.23741847

citation("ForestFireR")

The package implements the model analysed in Saravia, L.A. and de la Fuente, R., Dynamics of invasion in forest-fire models (manuscript; analysis code at https://github.com/EcoComplex/InvasionForestFiresBistability). Cite the package for the implementation and the article for the model.

Layout

  • R/model.R – the model reference page (help("ForestFireR-model")).
  • R/rates.R – xi2lambda(), eta2lambda(), default_rates().
  • R/simulate.R – landscape generation, the three simulation engines, FF_STATE.
  • R/movie.R – simulate_spatial_movie().
  • src/forest_fire_model.cpp – the C++ engine (lattice Gillespie dynamics, well-mixed Gillespie dynamics, mean-field integration) and the Rcpp export layer.
  • inst/examples/ – worked scripts.
  • tests/testthat/ – unit tests.
